blogs.title: The Word 'Need': When Does a Request Become a Command?
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Seventh Circuit's treatment of 'voluntariness' in consent searches, focusing specifically on the linguistic nuance of Officer Kizer's statement: 'I’m sensing that we almost need to come inside.' The author will explore the tension between a police officer's expression of urgent concern and the legal threshold for coercion, discussing how the court's 'totality of the circumstances' approach minimizes the impact of suggestive language when the subject has previously demonstrated the ability to refuse entry.

blogs.title: From Welfare Check to Evidence: The Elasticity of the 'Scope of Consent'
blogs.description: This post examines the 'objective reasonableness' standard used to determine the scope of a consent search. It will discuss whether a consent given for the narrow purpose of a safety check (ensuring children are okay) reasonably extends to a full sweep of the home, the location of other adults, and the questioning of residents. The post will consider the doctrinal implications of allowing 'safety checks' to serve as a gateway for broader investigations that eventually lead to warrant-based seizures.

blogs.title: Shared Spaces, Divided Rights: Third-Party Consent in Domestic Violence Calls
blogs.description: This post focuses on the application of third-party consent under Matlock and Cellitti within the volatile context of domestic violence. It will discuss the legal complications that arise when one spouse consents to police entry while the other spouse is the target of the investigation. The author will analyze whether the inherent pressure of a domestic dispute should heighten the scrutiny of 'voluntary' consent given by a victim or witness to police officers.
